data.name: describe_phenotype
data.rationale: Visual confirmation of mid-dose nuclear phenotype vs DMSO.

data.name: describe_phenotype
data.summary: Microscopist on 4 field(s): density similar vs DMSO; 8 observations; candidates: Aurora kinase inhibitors, unknown

observations.finding: Treated interphase monolayer slightly less dense with larger cell footprints and more open space than dense uniform DMSO monolayer.
Treated interphase monolayer slightly less dense with larger cell footprints and more open space than dense uniform DMSO monolayer. Cell spread area increased.
Nuclei (DAPI blue in composite) appear enlarged and more elongated vs DMSO; mean nuclear area visibly larger.
Nuclei (DAPI blue) enlarged, modestly more elongated: nuc_major_axis 41.4 vs 36.7 DMSO and nuc_solidity 0.975 vs 0.973 consistent with larger smooth oval nuclei.

Occasional very large flat polyploid/binucleate cells visible only in treated (e.g. f_62d6e00493cd bottom-center large polygonal cell with 2 nuclei, f_5cc69d7e1fd7 bottom-right large cell) consistent with fraction of large nuclei.
DAPI integrated intensity not reliably quantified from blue composite alone, but treated nuclei appear on average brighter / more DNA content, consistent with measured nuc_dna_integrated 501 vs 327.
Actin (red in composite) remains cortical/peripheral with no obvious fragmentation, aggregates or loss of stress fibers; subtle smoother texture only.

Tubulin (green in composite) remains filamentous interphase network, perinuclear enrichment preserved; no gross destabilizer loss or stabilizer bundling, no increase in mitotic spindles visible in composites.

notable_cells.why: Very large flat polygonal cell with expanded green tubulin cytoplasm and two adjacent DAPI foci - example of enlarged/polyploid cell driving increased cell_area and frac_large_nucleus.
Very large spread cell with single huge diffuse DAPI nucleus and extensive red cortical actin - example of increased cell_major_axis / nuc_area.

candidate_mechanisms.why: Huge nuclear area z=23.6, increased nuc major axis z=12, increased integrated DNA z=5.6 and cell area z=5.4 with more large nuclei and intact interphase microtubules/actin is classic Aurora B failure of cytokinesis / polyploidy phenotype; no evidence for actin disruptor, microtubule destabilizer/stabilizer or Eg5 monopolar mitotic arrest in composites.

Alternative generic Kinase inhibitors / DNA replication stress can also enlarge nuclei but images alone without mitotic index do not exclude; no gross cytoskeletal collapse to support actin or microtubule MoA.

report.uncertainty: Only RGB composites without DNA-normalized grayscale; tubulin/actin intensity and mitotic spindle morphology difficult to assess; integrated DNA z-score cannot be precisely verified by eye.

data.name: describe_phenotype
data.rationale: Visual confirmation of high-dose cytoskeletal disruption.

data.name: describe_phenotype
data.summary: Microscopist on 2 field(s): density lower vs DMSO; 7 observations; candidates: Microtubule stabilizers

observations.finding: Treated fields f_3a9d277bb2ef and f_c70a6182913f show markedly lower confluency and more isolated, well-spread cells than DMSO control f_bd4169e2e78f which is a dense, confluent epithelial sheet. Treated cells are stellate/spread vs compact polygonal in control.

Read from green in composite: tubulin intensity is brighter and more filamentous in treated cells. Prominent radial microtubule bundles extend to cell periphery with high contrast and sharp filament detail. Control shows dimmer, more diffuse green with lower filament contrast.
Increased tubulin texture variation - higher standard deviation and GLCM contrast, visible as coarse, bundle-like texture vs uniform haze in control.

Read from red in composite: F-actin (cortical/cytoplasmic red) still present, not collapsed. Edge/cortical staining appears sharper with higher contrast and higher standard deviation than control's more uniform red.

Read from blue in composite: nuclei mostly round/oval, blue DAPI. Overall nuclear number reduced proportional to cell loss. Small subset of enlarged/irregular nuclei visible in treated fields; no extensive multinucleation or fragmentation field-wide at this resolution.
Mean cell area appears larger and more spread, increasing cell-to-nucleus area ratio vs compact control cells. Consistent with spreading morphology, not cell rounding/shrinkage.
No field-wide loss/depolymerization of microtubules; microtubule network is retained and enhanced. Argues against destabilizer phenotype.

notable_cells.why: Field as a whole: sparse cells with bright radial green microtubule arrays vs dense control
Central cluster shows same bright, high-contrast green bundles and spread morphology

candidate_mechanisms.why: Increased tub_mean z=13.02 (0.416 vs 0.284), tub_std z=14.20, tub_glcm_contrast z=25.13 (0.004 vs 0.002) matches visible brighter, more filamentous, higher-contrast microtubules with bundles. Reduced cell_count z=-6.75 (99 vs 316) and increased frac_large_nucleus z=6.32 and cell_nuc_area_ratio z=5.19 consistent with mitotic arrest/polyploidy from stabilized microtubules. Actin changes secondary (act_glcm_contrast z=14.45, act_std z=7.05) without actin collapse.

report.uncertainty: Only RGB composites at screening resolution; no separate grayscale channels, no high-magnification spindle morphology to definitively distinguish stabilizer from other mitotic Kinase/Aurora/Eg5 inhibitors, but increased tubulin polymer mass strongly favors stabilizer over destabilizer/actin-disruptor.

data.rationale: Mid doses show dose-dependent nuclear/DNA increase with G2 arrest signature and 0.969 DNA-damage atlas match; high-dose tubulin bundling is isolated terminal toxicity with paradoxically decreased mitosis.

data.critique: Top call is supported: at 0.3-3 uM nuclear area/DNA rise strongly (z up to +26.6/+14.0) with tubulin near baseline and frac_mitotic_like depressed, matching DNA-damage atlas neighbours (0.969 top hit; 5/10) over DNA replication (lower similarities) and arguing against Aurora/Eg5/microtubule mitotic arrest. The 10 uM microtubule-stabilizer atlas signal is terminal and isolated: cell count collapses, nuclear DNA effect disappears and mitosis stays low, so it is better explained as high-dose toxicity than the primary MoA. Effects are single-replicate but very large across hundreds of cells, and p=0.68 is appropriately hedged versus DNA replication at 0.20. Budget is exhausted and no remaining free analysis is likely to overturn this dose-resolved pattern.

data.note: Reflection: Correct DNA damage call for mitomycin C (PubChem CID 5746, ChEMBL CHEMBL105 DNA inhibitor, e22). Mid-dose (0.3, 3 µM) phenotype was classic DNA damage: nuc_area z=23.6-26.6, nuc_dna_integrated z=5.6-14.0, frac_large_nucleus z=4.3-8.4 with increased cell area and decreased mitosis (frac_mitotic_like z -3.8), consistent with G2 arrest. Atlas confirmed: leaves-one-compound-out neighbors DNA damage 5/10, similarity 0.969 to chlorambucil and 0.93 to etoposide (e12), vs DNA replication camptothecin. High-dose 10 µM secondary tubulin bundling (tub_glcm_contrast z=25, tub_mean z=13) matched microtubule stabilizers epothilone/taxol at 0.895 (e13) but was isolated terminal toxicity with paradoxical mitotic suppression, not dose-progressive (tub_mean rho not predictive, e17). Literature supports: mitomycin C forms mono- and interstrand crosslinked DNA adducts repaired by UvrABC (PMID 20647419) and cytotoxic crosslinking activity (PMID 35349830).
